pages.text: "Just the broth!" Gugu, the broad-chested pigeon, pushed the carrots, beans, and potatoes to the edge of the bowl. Slurp, slurp! Steam rose over the long table by the stove.
"Chewing the bits is too much bother!" Gugu drank the broth and hopped up. "I will play outside until sunset!" Nono, the smallest, roundest sparrow, and Kiki, the pointy-eared cat, ate the bits too.
Outside, Gugu shivered at once. Fingertips stung, and a tummy rumbled. "Why am I cold already?"
"Come sit here, Gugu. Beside the stove is warmest." Grandpa Badger set two bowls side by side. Gugu stepped onto the threshold and looked inside.
The bottom of Nono's bowl was clear. Gugu's was hidden under food. "Broth warms you for a little while. Eating the bits keeps you warm longer."
Grandpa ladled food into Gugu's bowl. "One carrot, one bean, one potato. The bits too—yum!" Nono and Kiki raised their spoons. "The bits too—yum!"
Gugu chewed a piece of carrot. "Oh! It is sweet!" The beans and potatoes were tasty too, much richer than the broth. "The bits too—yum!"
Now the bowl's bottom showed. Gugu felt warm inside. "Now you can play for a long time." Grandpa smiled. Gugu touched the green bag strap and hopped.
Soup came again the next day. Gugu emptied the bowl. "One, slurp the broth! Two, scoop the bits! Three, eat until the bottom shows!" They played until sunset.
Nono and Kiki hugged Gugu from either side. Eating the bits keeps you warm for longer. "To the bottom tomorrow too! The bits too—yum!" Gugu beamed.
